question: Related Questions Q. There is a cash inheritance to be divided between 4 brothers and 4 sisters. 5th brother died before our mother leaving one son behind. We all are 4 brothers and a sister. 2 of my brothers want to use the inherited property and its belonging, until the division is performed 1549 views Q. Gold ornaments given to mother and after her death can the same son claim it back or steal without telling elders and father who is caretaker 8824 views Q. Inheritance 1632 views Q. Assalaamaliakum One of my friend aged around 40yrs had been married few months back & died in road accident after about 6 months of married life & they have no children.Iddat peroid of his wife has been over. My friend has 3 brothers & two sisters one married & the other a widow who stays with brothers as her daughters have been married off. Pl let us know what share does my friends wife get as my friend belongs to AhleHadis & how to share the property, 1434 views Q. 11th October 2010 / 2nd Zul Qadah 1431 Assalamou alaikum Respected Mufti sahib, I live in England, United Kingdom. I am a widow, my husband passed away nearly 3 months ago. I have 9 sons and 2 daughters. My husband?s mother is also alive. My late husband was the owner of two houses. Some months prior to his death, my husband made me a joint owner in one of these properties. Upon the instructions of my late husband, a solicitor completed the legal paperwork and we both signed various documents in the presence of witnesses. After the death of my husband, my children requested a scholar to explain the rules of Islamic inheritance so we could distribute my husband?s wealth according to the Shariah. When the discussion arose about the joint ownership of one of the houses, the scholar was of the opinion that this transfer of joint ownership was not valid because it seemed to him that this was only done symbolically and not as a genuine gift. However, beside the legal paperwork there is no other document available to support or negate the intention of the deceased. The scholar also said that even if the above gift was genuine, this kind of gift is faasid because of the following rule of Hiba: ومن وهب شقصاً مشاعاً فالهبة فاسدةٌ، فإن قسمه وسلمه جاز ) الهداية شرح بداية المبتدي,ص225,ج3, الناشر المكتبة الإسلامية) Which in essence says, if the item is such that if it is divided it can still be of use, then it is not permissible to give it without dividing it. Such items are ?a plot of land, a big house...?. See Bahishti Zewar (link below) page 66 point 5 http://www.islamicbulletin.org/free_downloads/women/bahishti_4_5_6_7.pdf I would be grateful if you would clarify (a) whether a house in the UK falls within the category of divisible property; (b) whether according to the Shariah I am the rightful owner of 50% of the house which was in joint ownership between myself and my husband. answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Inheritance & Will Question ID: 45536 Country: India Title: sharing of property Question: What is the ratio of distribution of property as per Islamic Shariah my father died on 02/01/1995 my mother died on 30/09/1983 we are 3 brothers and 5 sisters from my father’s first marriage after our mother died my father got second marriage and from second marriage he had one daughter, at the time of my father death we were 3 brothers 5 sisters and my father second wife and her daughter were alive. My father has left some properties which we want to sell and share the amount among us, how should it be distributed between 3 brothers 5 sister and my father’s second wife and her daughter what is the ratio in Islam? Answer ID: 45536 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 870/870/M=1434) In the above mentioned case the whole property of your father shall be divided into 96 shares. Out of which 12 shares shall go to your step mother (the second wife of your father) and 7 shares to her daughter while 14-14 shares to each brother and 7-7 shares to each sister. The detail of division is as follows: Details: Wife: 1x12 = 12 Sons: 3x14 = 42 Daughters: 6x07 = 42 Total: 96 Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
